articles.title: NCAA Men's Soccer Tournament Sees Parity Reign Supreme
articles.summary: With seven different national champions emerging since Stanford's three-peat in 2017, the NCAA men's soccer tournament has been dominated by parity over the past decade.
articles.content: The NCAA men's soccer tournament has been dominated by parity over the past decade, with seven different national champions emerging since Stanford's three-peat in 2017. Clemson stands out as an exception to this trend, having claimed back-to-back titles in 2021 and 2023. However, five teams have broken through to win their first national championship during this period, including last year's winner Washington and Vermont in 2024. Several schools are poised to capitalize on this parity trend, with SMU being a prime candidate after its strong start to the season. The Mustangs had been ranked number one in the polls before losing to North Carolina in the ACC championship game, but they have experience reaching the NCAA semifinals twice, albeit without achieving ultimate success. Top-ranked programs still seeking their first national title include Portland, West Virginia, and Creighton, all of which finished the regular season highly ranked. These teams possess the talent and potential to make a deep run through the bracket and claim their first championship. The excitement is building as the NCAA men's soccer tournament heats up in Cary. Fans can catch every game on various TV channels and streaming platforms, ensuring they don't miss a single moment of action. ESPNU will broadcast select games, while the ESPN app offers live streams for all matches. Additionally, Fubo will also air some games, making it easy to follow your favorite teams from anywhere in the world. To access these broadcasts, viewers can download the ESPN app or subscribe to Fubo's services. The semifinals and championship game will be broadcast on ESPNU, with simultaneous live streaming available on Fubo. This comprehensive coverage ensures that spectators can stay up-to-date with all the latest developments throughout the tournament. For those interested in watching without cable, the ESPN app offers a range of sports programming, including NBA, NFL, MLB, NHL, college sports, and more. With its user-friendly interface, viewers can access their favorite shows, such as SportsCenter and First Take, at any time or location. articles.title: Andrew Garfield Portrays Sam Altman in Biopic Artificial
articles.summary: The film focuses on OpenAI and its CEO, exploring his relationships and the power struggle over artificial intelligence.
articles.content: Actor Andrew Garfield has taken on the role of Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, in the biopic Artificial. The film's release is set for December 25, and it will likely be a challenging portrayal given that audiences may already have formed negative opinions about Altman. To prepare for the part, Garfield saw the challenge as an exciting opportunity rather than a daunting one. He aimed to get beyond his own preconceptions of Altman and understand him on a deeper level. As he delved into the character's world, Garfield's perspective on Altman began to shift. The biopic focuses on the rise of OpenAI and the intense pursuit of success that defined Altman's tenure as CEO. His relationships, particularly with cofounder Ilya Sutskever, are a central part of the story. The film also explores the power struggle over artificial intelligence in Silicon Valley. Garfield's goal as an actor is to uncover the core essence of his characters and merge it with his own being. He believes that every person has multiple facets, and Altman was no exception. To fully embody the character, Garfield worked on transforming his physical appearance, including his weight, gait, and voice. The resemblance between Garfield and Altman is striking, from his bouncy stride to his distinctive speech pattern. The actor's transformation down to the subtle nuances in his eyes showcases his impressive acting range. Garfield's portrayal of Sam Altman in 'Artificial' is a masterclass in subtlety, capturing the complexities of a multifaceted individual. To bring authenticity to his character, Garfield delved deep into Altman's psyche, seeking out qualities that resonated with him on a fundamental level. This introspective approach paid off, resulting in an uncannily believable performance that defies categorization. The actor acknowledged the weight of responsibility that comes with portraying a real person, particularly someone alive and within his own age group. He took this duty seriously, recognizing the importance of scrutinizing the individuals who wield significant influence over our world's trajectory. Garfield emphasized the role of storytellers in reflecting the times they live in, suggesting that examining human beings is an essential part of capturing the essence of their era. By probing the intricacies of personal relationships and inner lives, he aimed to shed light on those who shape our cultural landscape. The film 'Artificial' presents a somber portrayal of OpenAI's ascent, raising questions about moral accountability and safety concerns as its protagonists navigate the company's rapid growth. A blend of dark satire and levity adds nuance to the narrative, inviting viewers to ponder the long-term implications of emerging technologies. In one pivotal scene, Sutskever draws a humorous analogy between AI and artificial general intelligence, likening the latter to rocket ships in comparison to scooters. His wry remark elicits laughter from the audience, momentarily lightening the mood amidst more ominous explorations of technology's impact on society. Director Luca Guadagnino's filmic approach to OpenAI's story in Artificial echoes his previous work, where character-driven narratives take center stage. His films are known for their deliberate pacing and close-up shots that intensify emotional moments. In Artificial, Guadagnino employs a similar technique to convey the high stakes involved in pivotal scenes. Guadagnino's focus on people rather than technology is evident in his statement: "It's never about the object; it's always about the people." He highlights the conflict between individuals with differing worldviews, which ultimately drives the plot. The director's aim is not to delve into the intricacies of AI or AGI but to explore the human aspects that underpin these technological advancements. Guadagnino also emphasizes the allure of technology as a means to gain power and become self-entitled. He notes that even the prospect of an incredible technology can be misused, turning it into an instrument for personal gain rather than a force for good. This commentary on human nature adds depth to the narrative. The film's portrayal of bold personalities is reminiscent of The Social Network, where Garfield played Eduardo Saverin. However, Artificial takes a darker and more existential tone, delving into technical territory that sets it apart from its predecessor. Both films share an interest in forceful characters who shape the tech industry. Guadagnino's narrative approach allows for a nuanced exploration of human conflict and the consequences of technological advancements. By focusing on people rather than technology, he creates a more relatable and thought-provoking story that invites audiences to reflect on the implications of these developments. As Garfield delved into the world of tech moguls and emerging technologies, he couldn't help but wonder what it takes to succeed in today's late-stage capitalist society. He mused about the toll that immense power and possibility can take on an individual, leaving them vulnerable to being consumed by their own ambitions. The light-hearted moments in the film were provided by Ike Barinholtz's portrayal of Elon Musk as a self-absorbed figure who saunters into rooms with little regard for others. This comedic approach effectively highlighted the absurdity that comes with perceived importance and status, often met with laughter from the audience. Garfield acknowledged the public's fascination with cultural icons like Altman, who are shaping our future and leading us into a new era of culture and society. He noted that these figures often exhibit traits reminiscent of adolescence, such as being stuck in an early developmental phase, which Luca Guadagnino aimed to capture in his storytelling. Guadagnino's approach to the film was influenced by classic coming-of-age stories like John Hughes' films, blending high school comedy with higher stakes and a touch of sci-fi. This unique blend allowed the filmmakers to explore the adolescent mindset of their characters, who are navigating the complexities of growing up amidst rapidly changing technologies. The director's vision brought a new perspective to the story, one that focused on the relatable struggles and insecurities of these high-stakes figures rather than just their technological advancements. Garfield's portrayal of Altman is meticulous in its details, from his casual seating arrangements to his fashion choices during conversations about OpenAI's future. We had access to information not readily available to the public through our consultants and researchers who worked closely with us on the project, providing insight into the characters' lives. The film raises important questions about where society is heading and whether its leaders are equipped to navigate these uncharted territories, particularly when it comes to AI's far-reaching implications. Amidst this weighty exploration of AI's consequences, Artificial paints a haunting portrait of the individuals shaping our world. Garfield saw an opportunity in playing Altman, a figure who remains somewhat enigmatic despite his prominence, and he seized it with a sense of curiosity and wonder, driven by a desire to truly understand this complex individual. articles.summary: A rare air alert was sounded in Kaliningrad after reports emerged of an object entering Russian airspace from Lithuania.
articles.content: A rare air alert has been sounded in Kaliningrad, a Russian exclave situated between Poland and Lithuania. The alert was issued by the local governor, who reported that a suspicious object had been detected coming from the direction of Lithuania. The incident occurred hours after a drone strike targeted a Russian cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland, causing it to catch fire as it made its way towards Kaliningrad. The region is home to Russia's Baltic Fleet, and the naval base at Baltiysk is a key facility for the fleet. Photos taken by witnesses show what appears to be drone activity around the city of Baltiysk. However, the authenticity of these images has not been confirmed by independent sources. The air alert in Kaliningrad was activated after reports emerged that an object had entered Russian airspace from Lithuania, prompting authorities to sound the alarm in the Nemansky district near the border with Lithuania. Residents of Baltiysk took to Russian Telegram channels to share their experiences of air defenses being activated in the city during the night. They posted photos and videos showing bright streaks against the dark sky, accompanied by crackling sounds that echoed through the night. Kaliningrad authorities swiftly debunked a photo circulated online as allegedly depicting clouds of smoke rising from Baltiysk into the night sky. The image showed an orange haze on the horizon, but officials assured Russian state media it had no connection to the region. No casualties or damage were reported in Kaliningrad as of Sunday morning, according to Russian authorities. This development came amidst ongoing concerns and speculations surrounding the drone attack on a Russia-bound ship in the Gulf of Finland earlier that day. Lithuania's Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys firmly rejected claims suggesting the country's involvement in the alleged drone attack against Kaliningrad. He stated categorically that Lithuania has never authorized the use of its airspace for attacks targeting Russian Federation territories, including this specific case. Emergency services in Finland scrambled to put out a fire on the Russian cargo ship Sparta II after it drifted into Finnish territorial waters following an attack. The contents of the ship's cargo remain unknown, but the crew has been safely transferred to a Russian rescue vessel, according to the Finnish Border Guard. The boat will be moved out of Finnish waters once the fire is extinguished. Finland and Russia have both hinted that Ukrainian drones were responsible for the attack on the Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland. articles.title: Shuri Castle Main Hall Reopens After Devastating Fire
articles.summary: The main hall of Okinawa's Shuri Castle has been officially restored and reopened after a devastating fire seven years ago.
articles.content: A major milestone has been reached in the restoration of Okinawa's cultural heritage site, Shuri Castle, with the reopening of its main hall following a devastating fire seven years ago. The castle's main hall was officially restored and reopened on Sunday, its distinctive deep red exterior and intricate dragon ornaments now once again proudly on display. The ceremony, attended by local officials and residents, marked a significant moment in the recovery process for this iconic symbol of Okinawan culture. Strong winds had hampered the efforts of firefighters battling the blaze that destroyed parts of the castle complex back in 2019. The fire, which occurred during a festival at the castle, was particularly devastating due to its impact on the island's cultural heritage and the fact that it took nearly 12 hours for firefighters to bring under control. Despite an extensive investigation, the cause of the blaze could not be determined, but an electrical fault is believed to have been the most likely explanation. At a ceremony held in the castle courtyard outside the main hall, Okinawa Gov. Genta Koja reflected on the significance of this milestone, stating "The fire was a tremendous shock to the Okinawan people" and expressing his own deep sense of pride and relief at seeing the restoration finally complete. The restored Seiden hall is a testament to Okinawa's resilience in the face of adversity. The castle's history dates back to 1992 when it was reconstructed for the island's reversion to Japan, marking the end of its 27-year US occupation. Historians and artisans from across Japan played a crucial role in the restoration process, working alongside local experts and donors from around the world. Their tireless efforts have finally borne fruit with the opening of Seiden hall to the public, bringing a sense of closure to the islanders who suffered greatly during World War II. The 2019 fire that ravaged Shuri Castle was a devastating blow, destroying four nearby structures and heavily damaging two others in addition to Seiden and two adjacent halls. The castle's restoration is being carried out in stages, with some experts predicting it may take over a decade to complete. While the opening of Seiden hall marks an important milestone, work on other parts of the castle remains ongoing. Historian Kurayoshi Takara was instrumental in ensuring that the new main hall accurately reflects the original building's design, incorporating fresh findings from historical documents and archaeological research. The restored main hall has been painstakingly recreated to match its pre-war appearance as closely as possible, with every detail meticulously considered to ensure authenticity. This dedication to preserving Okinawa's cultural heritage is a beacon of hope for the islanders who have worked tirelessly towards this goal. The restoration of Shuri Castle's hall has been a long and arduous process, but it has finally paid off with the recreation of its signature deeper red color. Artisans were able to recreate the pigment by blending a commercial product with one derived from iron bacteria found in northern Okinawa. This innovative solution was the result of extensive research and experimentation. The painstaking effort is a testament to the dedication of those involved in preserving Okinawa's cultural heritage. Shuri Castle, now restored to its former glory, is poised to become an even more significant tourist attraction, potentially boosting Okinawa's economy and drawing in more visitors to the island. articles.title: French lawmakers demand end to police use of tear gas
articles.summary: A growing concern is being raised over the potential impact of tear gas on reproductive health.
articles.content: French lawmakers and activists have joined forces to demand an end to the use of tear gas by police following recent protests. The growing concern centers on its potential impact on menstrual cycles and reproductive health, although a direct medical link has yet to be established. Tear gas was deployed during student demonstrations over living costs, some of which turned violent. Women who were exposed reported experiencing painful cramps, unexpected bleeding, and disrupted periods. An advocacy group has collected over 10,000 complaints from individuals who claim to have suffered similar symptoms after exposure to tear gas. Opposition lawmakers are pushing for a ban on the use of tear gas and independent research into its potential health effects. They argue that there is a pressing need to investigate any possible connections between tear gas and reproductive health issues. The government has not yet committed to these demands, however. The Interior Minister has defended the continued use of tear gas as an essential tool for crowd control. He views it as a safer alternative to other methods of dispersing crowds, which could be more hazardous. His stance is at odds with those who are calling for an immediate halt to its use. Tear gas grenades used by French police contain CS, a chemical irritant that affects the eyes, skin, and respiratory system. When inhaled or ingested, it can cause irritation and discomfort. The extent of its effects depends on the amount used and duration of exposure. Thousands of people in France have been exposed to tear gas during recent protests, including children, pregnant women, and older individuals living near protest sites. Photographers Mélina Galland and Chloé Baroux are among those who claim their menstrual cycles were disrupted after being exposed to the chemical irritant. Galland, 24, was working as an independent photographer on October 17 in Paris when tear gas grenades were fired. She wore multiple masks but still experienced intense belly pain that evening. Chloé Baroux, also a photographer, noticed irregular periods and menstrual pain after covering protests against a security bill in 2020 and 2021. Initially, her cycles returned to normal, but she has since experienced irregularities again, this time linked to recent exposure during the current protests. Eva-Luna Tholance, a former journalist who investigated potential effects of tear gas on reproductive health six years ago, is now raising awareness through her advocacy group "Lacrymos de sang" ("Tears of blood"). The organization has been collecting accounts from people who claim to have experienced symptoms after being exposed to tear gas. The group's questionnaire, sent out last month, gathered descriptions of exposure and symptoms but does not provide a comprehensive picture of the issue. The accounts were not reviewed by independent medical professionals, leaving many questions unanswered about the prevalence and severity of symptoms among those affected. The French group's questionnaire has revealed a disturbing trend among women who have been exposed to tear gas during protests. Some people experience mild cramps, but a significant number report experiencing severe menstrual pain that is far worse than their usual periods. Reports of bleeding range from light spotting to extremely heavy bleeding lasting several days, with some individuals even experiencing prolonged bleeding that persists for weeks. The phenomenon has raised concerns about the potential impact of tear gas on reproductive health, particularly in women who are postmenopausal or taking hormonal contraception that normally prevents menstrual bleeding. A recent study collected accounts of symptoms reported after the 2020 Black Lives Matter protests and found a possible link between exposure to tear gas and adverse reproductive health outcomes. The limitations of past research on tear gas may explain why its impact on menstrual health has gone unreported until now, according to experts. Most studies on tear gas were conducted in controlled environments involving healthy young men in military settings. French law enforcement's primary suppliers of tear gas grenades, Alsetex and Nobel Sport, declined to comment on the potential link between tear gas exposure and reproductive health issues. The Interior Ministry disputes this association, stating that no scientific studies have proven CS gas causes menstrual changes or miscarriages. The ministry has carried out research in 2021 and 2022 focusing on individual exposure to tear gas among law enforcement personnel but refused to share any findings with the public. It acknowledged, however, that some symptoms affecting the skin and eyes can persist for longer than just a few hours. This pattern suggests a recurring issue with companies offering long-term voyages on ships designed as permanent residences. The Victoria Cruises Line had planned to launch the Victoria Majestic in 2023, promoting it as a yearslong journey around the world for those seeking a life at sea. The vessel was marketed as a place where people could live on permanently. Concerned investors who had put down deposits with Victoria in 2024 requested refunds when they began to doubt whether the cruise would ever set sail; by November, the ship remained docked and had not embarked on its maiden voyage. Mikael Petterson, cofounder of Villa Vie, reflected on his efforts to keep the Odyssey sailing in an interview this week. He expressed his unwavering commitment to ensuring the cruise continued on its journey. His personal investment and dedication were evident in his words. He stated that he would have done anything to salvage the situation. The Odyssey had been a flagship for Villa Vie, offering residents a unique lifestyle at sea. Despite initial concerns from some investors, many remained committed to their dream of living on board. The Cassinghams, one such couple, had invested heavily in the venture and were eager to see it succeed. They had sold their home in Colorado to fund their deposit on the Majestic. The Odyssey's itinerary underwent significant changes during its final months at sea. Services began to deteriorate, and residents faced increased cash calls as Villa Vie struggled with cash flow issues. The company cited rising fuel prices as a major contributing factor to these problems. Despite these challenges, many residents remained resolute in their commitment to the lifestyle. Villa Vie's operations came to a halt in October 2024 when the company suspended activities due to financial difficulties. In response, Victoria Cruises Lines issued a statement on its blog, outlining the conditions under which it would resume sailing. According to the statement, the Odyssey would not set sail until 80% of its cabins had been sold. The financial woes of Villa Vie had been building for some time, ultimately leading to a suspension of operations in Cambodia on October 27th, leaving residents stranded without a clear plan for their future. Cassinghams, who had previously expressed enthusiasm for the Odyssey's concept, were now facing the reality of being stuck in Cambodia after disembarking from the ship. Their love for travel was hindered by the logistics of airlines and airports, as they had mentioned earlier. Holly Hennessy, a 70-year-old woman, had also been drawn to Villa Vie's promise of a mobile life at sea. Having spent her retirement savings on plans to sail around the world with Victoria Majestic, she was undeterred by that setback and instead turned her attention to the Odyssey. Hennessy's experiences aboard the Odyssey were bittersweet, as she reflected on the time she had spent there before being forced to disembark last month. Thomas's thoughts on the cruise lifestyle were shaped by its promise of a carefree existence, free from the burdens of daily life. The ship's departure was delayed for months after its initial planned May 2024 launch, sparking a sense of familiarity for Thomas, who had invested in Villa Vie's Odyssey. This déjà vu feeling likely stemmed from her past experiences with the cruise lifestyle. Months later, on September 30, 2024, the vessel finally set sail. Now, Thomas finds herself living out of a hotel in Cambodia while trying to bring her pets along before the holidays. The prolonged delays and failed ventures have left Thomas with feelings of resentment towards those who sold her the dream of life at sea. articles.title: Research Project on Alzheimer's Disease Among African Americans Terminated by Trump Administration
articles.summary: The study, which aimed to identify risk factors for Alzheimer's in African Americans, has been abruptly cancelled by the Trump administration.
articles.content: A research project focused on uncovering the reasons behind the higher incidence of Alzheimer's disease among African Americans has been abruptly terminated by the Trump administration. The study was conducted in a predominantly Black neighborhood in Pittsburgh, where participants underwent memory tests, sleep and blood pressure tracking, and shared their life stories to help researchers identify potential risk factors for Alzheimer's. Researchers claim that the project's premature cancellation not only squandered over $8 million of taxpayer funds already invested but also left the study participants in limbo, without any knowledge about the results of their brain tests. Participants like Roderick Blair, who spent four years participating in the study, are now facing uncertainty and frustration. They came into our community, took everything from us, and then left us hanging, Blair said, expressing his concerns about the abrupt termination of the project. The distrust of U.S. health institutions within the Black community is a long-standing issue, rooted in historical racial disparities in healthcare, unequal access to medical care, and systemic biases within the nation's medical system. The Pittsburgh-based research study had made significant strides in bridging the trust gap between healthcare providers and the Black community by engaging local residents and encouraging open discussions about memory loss and dementia. This grassroots approach helped to dispel misconceptions and myths surrounding these conditions, with participants increasingly seeking information on how to identify and address them. In fact, Wagner reported that families who had previously dismissed memory loss as a sign of depression were now asking about dementia, while community members outside the study were inquiring about including their relatives. It's not surprising that many Black Americans hold misconceptions about memory loss, with over half believing it is a natural part of aging rather than a disease. This widespread misconception highlights the urgent need for targeted education and awareness campaigns to dispel these myths. Researchers pointed out that the project was unfairly stripped of funding by the National Institutes of Health, which deemed it "not science despite rigorous review and community input. According to Wagner, this decision was particularly galling given the study's focus on real-world issues affecting the Black community. The termination of research grants by the National Institutes of Health (NIH) has left many scientists scrambling to salvage their projects. For Negar Fani, a neuropsychologist at Emory University in Atlanta, the loss was particularly devastating as she had invested two years into a five-year study on how racial discrimination affects the brain and body of Black Americans. The NIH's decision to terminate Fani's $2.9 million grant has left her team struggling to explain their situation to participants who feel abandoned. The study had already enrolled 66 out of its planned 220 participants, but the NIH deemed it not scientific" and "subjective. This criticism is puzzling given that the research was initially approved and had a clear focus on real-world issues affecting Black communities. Fani's experience is not an isolated incident, as numerous researchers are finding themselves at odds with the NIH over grant funding. In one notable case, study lead researcher Andrea Rosso has joined a lawsuit against the NIH and its parent Department of Health and Human Services. The lawsuit is part of a growing body of legal actions taken by scientists who feel their work is being unfairly targeted. The criteria used to halt grants are often vague, but include descriptions that mention disparities", "minority" and "racial. These terms have become red flags for the administration, which has been actively hunting down and halting medical grants. As a result, researchers like Fani are left to pick up the pieces and try to find alternative funding to complete their studies. The lawsuit against HHS has gained more plaintiffs, including Ann Cohen, a prominent figure in Alzheimer's disease research. Her own study was halted after three years, despite having spent $5.2 million on it. The abrupt termination of her project raises an unsettling question: what to do with the blood samples collected from participants. Cohen's words echo through the debate: You lose trust a hell of a lot faster than you build it. Her concern is not unique, as many in the research community share similar fears about the erosion of public trust. The abrupt changes in funding priorities have created uncertainty and anxiety among researchers. The shift in priorities at NIH has been drastic, with 2,000 fewer grants awarded this year compared to last year's total. This means a $200 million reduction in funding for multiyear studies. The Association of American Medical Colleges report highlights the significant drop in research investments. The implications are far-reaching and concerning, especially considering the emphasis on rigorous research that will supposedly improve health outcomes. Jill Rosenthal, director of public health policy at the Center for American Progress, is vocal about her discontent with the new approach: Many decisions are based on political biases rather than evidence-based processes. Her critique underscores the perceived disconnect between research priorities and actual needs. The abrupt halt in funding for certain research projects has left scientists frustrated and concerned about the impact on public health. Resources are being squandered as valuable opportunities to find cures for diseases are being missed. Community trust is also at stake, particularly in Pittsburgh where researchers had built a decade-long relationship with study participants. The study's findings on Alzheimer's risk factors are now gathering dust, and the broken promises have eroded the trust that was carefully cultivated over years. Rebuilding this trust will be a long-term effort, as Blair, a study participant, acknowledged: It's going to take years to reestablish something that was moving pretty good." articles.title: Genesis Unveils Hybrid Powertrains for G80 and GV80 Models
articles.summary: The company has introduced hybrid vehicles at this year's LA Auto Show, with new powertrains offering improved efficiency and performance.
articles.content: Genesis has introduced its first hybrid vehicles at this year's LA Auto Show, unveiling new powertrains for the G80 sedan and GV80 SUV. The company claims that these electrified systems offer improved efficiency and performance compared to their non-hybrid counterparts. Growing interest in energy-efficient cars among American drivers is driving demand for hybrids and battery electrics, particularly as fuel costs continue to rise and consumers become more familiar with these technologies. One reason hybrids are gaining popularity is that they can be used just like traditional combustion cars, eliminating the need for home charging systems or adjustments to daily routines. The G80 Hybrid and GV80 Hybrid share a 2.5-liter turbocharged hybrid powertrain, which Genesis says delivers 16% more power than its gasoline-only equivalent. This system produces 347 horsepower and 391 pound-feet of torque, thanks in part to a new liquid-cooled battery pack that improves thermal management. The use of a liquid-cooled battery allows for higher maximum discharge rates compared to Hyundai Motor Group's previous air-cooled hybrid batteries, resulting in enhanced performance. Both models come equipped with a seven-speed automatic transmission adapted to work seamlessly with the electric motor's regenerative braking capabilities. Genesis has confirmed that it will be releasing an extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) next year, boasting a range of 640 miles and scheduled for arrival in early 2027. The fuel efficiency of Genesis' latest hybrids has been revealed, but not without some caveats. According to the company, the G80 Hybrid is 30% more efficient than its standard counterpart, while the GV80 Hybrid boasts a 24% improvement in this area. Based on current EPA estimates, it's likely that these vehicles will achieve around 30 mpg and 27 mpg respectively, although official ratings have yet to be confirmed. While any increase in efficiency is welcome, these gains may not be as significant as some might hope for. One potential perk of these hybrids is the ability to switch into a silent electric mode for short periods, ideal for gliding into driveways or parking decks without disturbing those nearby. However, it's worth noting that even when running on battery power alone, all energy must ultimately come from the gas tank. A new feature called Stay Mode allows owners to run climate control and infotainment systems without starting the engine for up to 30 minutes. This could be seen as a useful option for those who want to spend a little time relaxing in their vehicle before getting on with their day. The G80 and GV80 Hybrids are largely identical to their non-hybrid counterparts, aside from some minor tweaks such as a redesigned grille inlay and new exterior color options. The interior design of the Genesis hybrids features a prominent 27-inch OLED display that serves as both an instrument cluster and navigation system, stretching across nearly half of the dashboard. Genesis has incorporated various advanced technologies into its new models, including Digital Key 2 Premium, which enables owners to unlock and start their cars using their phones instead of traditional key fobs. Additionally, active road noise cancellation is available for a smoother driving experience. The brand's driver-assistance suite boasts impressive features such as Highway Drive Assist 2 steering assistance system and Remote Smart Parking Assist 2. The company has yet to announce pricing details for the sedan and SUV models. More information on specifications and EPA fuel economy figures will be released closer to the early 2027 launch date, when these vehicles are expected to hit the market. Genesis's move into hybrid territory is not without precedent, with Toyota having led the way since introducing the RX 400h in 2004. However, as an independent brand founded only in 2015, Genesis has been playing catch-up; nonetheless, its entry into the hybrid market brings it on par with other luxury brands that have recently updated their hybrids and meets growing customer demand for more fuel-efficient vehicles. The Genesis brand is expanding its reach in the US market, making its high-performance GV60 Magma full-electric SUV available in more states and regions due to higher-than-expected demand for this unique model. The company's decision to widen the availability of the GV60 Magma reflects a growing interest in luxury electric vehicles among consumers. This move is also likely to increase Genesis' market presence. At the LA Auto Show, Genesis executives provided a glimpse into the brand's future plans by announcing an upcoming extended-range EV that combines advanced plug-in hybrid technology with an onboard gasoline generator. Scheduled for launch in early 2027, this EREV model aims to achieve over 640 miles on a single charge before its battery and gas tank are depleted. The exact specifications of the new model remain unclear. Genesis has confirmed that it will continue to push the boundaries of innovation in the electric vehicle space. With the GV60 Magma and the upcoming EREV model, the brand is well-positioned to compete with other luxury brands in the market. articles.title: Zion National Park Adventure Takes Family in Place of Traditional Thanksgiving
articles.summary: A family of four spent their Thanksgiving holiday hiking and exploring Zion National Park, Utah, instead of cooking a traditional meal.
articles.content: I decided against joining my husband's family for Thanksgiving, opting instead for an adventure in Zion National Park, Utah. The decision was motivated by a desire to escape the usual holiday table dynamics, which had become increasingly difficult since my mother's passing two years prior. The idea of skipping cooking and embracing a new tradition resonated with my family, particularly my 12-year-old daughter. "Maybe we skip cooking and opt for an adventure" I suggested, to which they agreed without hesitation. We set off from our home in Oregon, bound for Las Vegas, where we rented a car and began the scenic drive to Zion National Park. The park's majestic red and orange rock formations were a major draw, but it was the promise of a cooler, sunnier climate that sealed the deal, late November proved to be an ideal time for hiking. The drive from St. George, where my family was staying, was short, but the shuttle ride into the park took longer than expected. We soon found ourselves among crowds of hikers from around the world, many of whom seemed just as eager to explore the park's trails as we were. As we prepared to hike The Narrows, a ranger explained that many visitors wear waterproof overalls for protection against the freezing water, which can rise from ankle- to neck-deep depending on how far you hike. The eight-mile stretch of the Virgin River through a gorge with towering rock walls was an adventure in itself, and renting equipment was made easy by the park's facilities. Each person was handed a five-foot-tall wooden pole to aid navigation over slippery rocks. A flash flood warning from the National Weather Service could prompt Zion to close The Narrows, but our group seemed undeterred by the risks. My husband grumbled about the cold, while our daughter begged him to reconsider, and I couldn't help but join in. We eventually found ourselves among crowds of hikers from around the world, all clad in heavy neoprene pants, waterproof socks, and boots, as we stepped into the frigid water on Thanksgiving morning. The murkiness of the water made footing a challenge for some, while others gazed up at the gleaming cliffsides dotted with pines, marveling at the beauty of the gorge. As we waded upstream, our fellow adventurers were just as captivated by the scenery as we were. Some exclaimed in different languages over the breathtaking views, their eyes fixed on the red and gold hues of the rock formations. The sense of community was palpable among these strangers-turned-traveling-companions, united by a shared desire to explore this natural wonder. The water temperature had dropped to 45˚F, but our spirits remained high as we navigated the treacherous terrain with our poles. It was clear that many visitors were just as eager to tackle The Narrows as we were, and the camaraderie among hikers added to the excitement of this unique adventure. The holiday hike was a respite from grief that had been weighing heavily on me after losing my mom. For three hours, I couldn't stop smiling as we navigated through the icy waters of Zion National Park's Narrows. The camaraderie among hikers added to the excitement of this unique adventure, making it feel like a perfect way to spend Thanksgiving. Gratitude overwhelmed me as I murmured thanks to the ravens soaring above us in the bright blue sky. We dined on veggie burgers and sweet potato fries that evening, reliving the highlights of our hike and comparing notes about hiking The Narrows with my husband and daughter. My family had decided to turn back after a mile of slogging through the river, while I was eager to keep walking and explore more of the park's wonders. "I wanted to keep going," I pointed out, as we shared stories over dinner and laughed together about our differing opinions on the best hike for the day. The deactivation of his account has left Khan searching for alternative employment opportunities. He has managed to secure work with Blacklane, a Berlin-based chauffeur service that he finds more manageable than Uber due to its supportive representatives. Khan's experience highlights the contradiction in Uber's decision to deactivate drivers who are still able and willing to work. articles.title: New Observations from James Webb Space Telescope Challenge Assumptions about Galaxies and Supermassive Black Holes
articles.summary: Astronomers are questioning the traditional understanding of how galaxies and supermassive black holes form after new observations revealed evidence that challenges the prevailing idea.
articles.content: A long-held assumption about the origins of galaxies and supermassive black holes has been turned on its head by new observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). The prevailing idea for decades was that galaxies formed first, with massive stars dying and leaving behind black holes that eventually merged to create enormous supermassive black holes. However, this theory is no longer considered a complete picture of the universe's evolution. According to Joseph Silk, an astrophysicist at Johns Hopkins University, the deaths of massive stars were thought to be responsible for creating the supermassive black holes found at the centers of most galaxies. But recent observations from JWST have revealed new evidence that is challenging this standard model. Astronomers are now left questioning which came first: the galaxies or their supermassive black hole residents, with some experts suggesting that the traditional understanding may be incomplete or even incorrect. The existence of supermassive black holes has long been a topic of fascination for astronomers. These behemoths reside at the centers of many galaxies, including our own Milky Way. However, new findings have raised intriguing questions about their origins and relationship with the galaxies they inhabit. Researchers have discovered that some supermassive black holes appear to be larger than expected, given the size of their host galaxies. For instance, a study published in the journal Nature measured the mass of a black hole in an object called Abell2744-QSO1 and found it to comprise most of its mass. This has led scientists to ponder where such massive black holes could have come from. Some experts suggest that supermassive black holes may be formed through the direct collapse of enormous gas clouds, which would grant them a head start in their growth. Others propose that these behemoths may be ordinary stellar remnants that grew at an unusually rapid pace. Maiolino outlined several possibilities, and it's possible that more than one explanation is correct. The dynamics between galaxies and supermassive black holes are complex, with both entities exerting influence on each other through gravitational forces. This cosmic tug of war has significant implications for our understanding of the universe, particularly in terms of how these massive objects interact and evolve over time. The relationship between black holes and galaxies is a complex one, with each influencing the other throughout their evolution. A growing black hole can have a profound impact on its host galaxy, releasing enormous amounts of energy that either heats or expels gas. This, in turn, can curb or shut down star formation. However, this process can also compress gas and potentially trigger new stars to form. The balance between these two processes varies depending on the type of galaxy, with some exhibiting "histories of extreme violence" due to their massive black holes. In contrast, galaxies like the Milky Way are more influenced by feedback from their stars. The debate over which came first - black holes or galaxies - remains unresolved, and it will require far more data from future missions like the James Webb Space Telescope to shed light on this question. Currently, astronomers have only a few dozen samples of objects to work with, which is not enough to determine whether oversized black holes are typical. The origins of the universe are still shrouded in mystery, and a crucial question remains unanswered: did black holes or galaxies come first? To shed light on this enigma, astronomers have been studying the relationship between the two, but their findings have only led to more questions. A key indicator of which came first would be whether black holes outweigh their host galaxies. If that's the case, it would suggest that black holes formed before galaxies, a notion that could challenge current understanding of cosmic evolution. On the other hand, if stars dominate over black holes in these distant systems, it would point to a different sequence. The debate highlights the complexity of the universe and its many mysteries waiting to be unraveled. As one expert noted, "Asking which came first may be too simplistic," and instead, astronomers might need to consider multiple pathways for the formation and evolution of black holes in various environments and cosmic epochs. articles.title: Max Verstappen Wins Las Vegas Grand Prix in Thrilling Contest
articles.summary: Red Bull's Max Verstappen emerged victorious after a closely contested race with Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli.
articles.content: The Las Vegas Grand Prix witnessed an unprecedented display of racing prowess, with Red Bull's Max Verstappen emerging victorious in a thrilling contest that saw 34 lead changes throughout the event. A tightly packed group of 10 cars dominated the majority of the race, with Verstappen and Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli engaging in a non-stop battle for the top spot. The intense competition resulted in a constant shifting of positions among the leaders, making it impossible to predict who would emerge victorious. Meanwhile, Verstappen's team was busy strategizing on how to optimize his car's electrical energy deployment, with their driver seemingly always one step ahead of his rivals. The drama reached its climax as Mercedes' challenge began to unravel in the final laps, with Russell making a critical error that led to a crash while attempting to pass Antonelli. The Mercedes team's momentum was already waning when Hamilton received a 10-second penalty for his own aggressive maneuver in a bid to pass Norris off-track. This infraction added to the team's woes, further complicating their efforts to regain the lead. The incident had been part of a heated battle for position that also involved Leclerc. The nature of this grand prix was unlike any other Formula 1 event, with its reliance on unique circumstances surrounding the Las Vegas circuit and the limitations imposed by energy-starved hybrid engines. This year's edition of the race seemed more akin to American oval racing than traditional F1 competition. The unorthodox conditions had created an unpredictable atmosphere. The city's reputation as a hub for entertainment was being matched only by the drama unfolding on its famous Strip. As Verstappen celebrated his victory, he reflected on the extraordinary nature of the event, drawing parallels with the legendary Monza slipstreaming battles of the 1960s and early 1970s. Verstappen's engineer Tom Hart aptly summarized the key to their success: "Yeah, and not many of them on the straight," he said, highlighting Verstappen's ability to reclaim the lead at the last corner, often by going around the outside. The high-stakes battle between Verstappen and Mercedes continued unabated, with both drivers trading positions throughout the grueling event. A mid-race safety car intervention did little to disrupt the momentum of the Dutch driver, who maintained his composure under intense pressure from behind. Meanwhile, Antonelli emerged as a new challenger for Verstappen's lead after initially starting sixth on the grid and making a series of daring overtakes to reach the top spot with just 12 laps remaining. As the Italian driver pushed Verstappen hard, it seemed that the Dutchman might finally be challenged for his position, but he proved once again why he is one of the most formidable drivers in the field. The final laps of the race saw a critical phase unfold as George Russell attempted to mount another challenge against Max Verstappen's lead. Russell made his move into Turn Five with just two laps remaining but unfortunately for him, he struggled to control his car over the bumps leading into the corner and locked up his brakes. This loss of traction sent Russell's car veering off course and into the barrier, causing significant damage and ending any hopes of a top-three finish. The chaos in the lead battle had been a defining feature of this grand prix from its early stages, with multiple drivers vying for top honors. Piastri's remarkable recovery to third place from his 17th starting position on the grid was one of the standout performances of the day, having started behind several other cars due to an engine penalty. Meanwhile Norris had initially slipped out of the top ten in the first part of the race, but managed to regain ground and finish a strong second behind Verstappen. The McLarens' late surge around Kimi Antonelli gave Verstappen crucial breathing space on the final lap. The final standings for this extraordinary race saw Pierre Gasly take sixth place, closely followed by Franco Colapinto in seventh position. Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari collided with another vehicle, resulting in an eighth-place finish, while Carlos Sainz also suffered a setback, securing ninth place. George Russell managed to hold onto tenth spot, rounding out the top ten. The season is now drawing to a close, and next up for Formula 1 will be the Qatar Grand Prix at the Lusail International Circuit from November 27-29. articles.title: Winter Damage Leaves Kyiv Residents Struggling with Replacement Windows
articles.summary: Kyiv residents are facing challenges finding replacement windows due to skilled installer shortages and government assistance delays, exacerbating the situation.
articles.content: As winter tightens its grip on Ukraine, Kyiv's residents are bracing for the cold, but many face an added challenge: finding replacement windows to seal out the chill. Russian missile and drone attacks have left a trail of destruction, with buildings damaged and families exposed to the elements. For Oleksandra Horban, the struggle is all too personal. Her apartment block was hit by a missile in October, leaving her small home shattered and vulnerable to the cold. Despite repeated cleaning efforts, tiny shards of glass still linger, posing a constant threat to her 2-year-old son's safety. The problem isn't unique to Horban's building, many Kyiv residents are struggling to find replacement windows as skilled installers become increasingly scarce. The shortage is exacerbated by government assistance that can take months to arrive, leaving families in limbo. As temperatures plummeted to minus 20 degrees Celsius last winter, the need for secure and warm homes became starkly apparent. But with costs soaring and skilled labor hard to come by, many low-income districts are feeling the pinch, particularly those near industrial zones where environmental degradation is a pressing concern. Horban's home, a Soviet-era "groundscraper, was hit particularly hard by the missile blast, which shattered hundreds of facade windows in a vertical section of apartments. The destruction has left residents like Horban facing an uphill battle to keep winter at bay. Fiberboard and tarps are being used to temporarily cover shattered windows in Horban's apartment complex. Some makeshift covers have small openings that allow daylight to filter in through Plexiglas panels. Replacing the broken windows would be a costly endeavor for many residents. The cost of new windows can exceed $1,700, an amount that far surpasses Ukraine's average salary. This leaves homeowners with limited financial resources struggling to afford repairs. The destruction caused by the war has resulted in significant housing damage. According to estimates, approximately 3 million housing units were destroyed or badly damaged by the end of last year. This extensive damage has contributed to a staggering $90 billion in reconstruction needs, as reported by the World Bank. Ukraine's window manufacturers are currently able to meet demand for replacement windows. However, the shortage of skilled installers remains a major bottleneck. Businesses have been unable to exempt their employees from military service, including many experienced installers who could be completing installations. The installation process itself can also be delayed due to high demand and shortages of materials. Factories are capable of manufacturing windows within 10 working days, but installation crews may take significantly longer to become available. Installation costs have at least doubled over the past year due to the intense competition for skilled laborers. The harsh winter conditions in Ukraine have been exacerbated by a shortage of skilled window installers, forcing workers to carry heavy materials up and down stairs without the aid of functioning elevators. As one installer recounted, he and his team made 18 trips up and down the stairs on a recent job, hauling heavy loads to replace balcony doors and windows in a fourth-floor apartment. They worked through power outages, refusing to wait for electricity to be restored before getting started. To address the shortage of skilled laborers, the window installation industry is investing heavily in training programs. A vocational college in Kyiv has recently opened a state-of-the-art facility funded by the European Union, where 26 10th graders are enrolled in a three-year program to become window, door and facade installers. The students practice their skills on mock window openings built from various materials, including brick, cinder block, wood, and synthetic materials. However, their classes are frequently disrupted due to missile and drone alerts, which have become a regular occurrence in the country. Instructor Volodymyr Tserbii hopes that his apprentices will play a crucial role in rebuilding Ukraine after the war, providing them with a much-needed skillset for reconstruction efforts. The daunting task of rebuilding Ukraine's shattered infrastructure will take a decade or more to complete, according to government estimates. For Horban, waiting for new windows is just one of many challenges her family faces. Her apartment lacks gas, forcing them to rely on portable cooking equipment and only heat their son's room when electricity permits. The kitchen roof has also been compromised by water damage. The trauma caused by the blast is evident in Horban's toddler son Viacheslav, who is increasingly familiar with the sounds of war. He frequently presses his nose against a surviving windowpane to wave at passersby and ask his mother about potential future bombings, using bam bam to describe explosions. Horban's words capture the bleak reality facing many Ukrainians: This is not life, this is surviving." articles.title: College football teams suffer unexpected losses in Week 12.
articles.summary: Several top-ranked teams fell to their opponents, leaving fans stunned and analysts searching for explanations.
articles.content: College football Week 12 was marked by unexpected outcomes, with several top-ranked teams falling victim to their opponents' determination and skill. While the schedule seemed relatively tame on paper, featuring only one ranked matchup among the many games played, the sport itself refused to disappoint. Top 10 teams dropped like dominoes, leaving fans stunned and analysts scrambling for explanations. In a surprising turn of events, No. 4 UCLA's loss to Michigan left Utah as the sole undefeated team in the Power Four conference. Meanwhile, No. 10 BYU narrowly escaped defeat at Kansas, requiring triple overtime to secure their win. The aftermath of Week 12 saw two of the CFP Top 10 teams fall and five top 25 teams suffer similar fates. No. 7 Miami also found itself locked in a tight contest but managed to keep its hopes for a two-bid ACC alive. Georgia's dominance continued, as they dismantled Shane Beamer and the No. 21 Gamecocks on the road with a commanding 34-6 victory. The Bulldogs' performance was marked by impressive numbers: 281 yards thrown, 140 yards rushed, and an astonishing 87 total yards surrendered by LaNorris Sellers. The Bulldogs' scoring spree saw them rack up 31 consecutive points from the two-minute mark of the third quarter onwards, leaving little doubt about their superiority. This victory marked another addition to Georgia's growing list of triumphs, with one notable exception, a bizarre loss to Auburn earlier in the season. Ohio State's struggling offense continued its dismal performance against Nebraska, amassing a meager 76 yards on the ground from 22 carries. Conversely, the Cornhuskers' rushing attack had a field day, notching an impressive 176 yards. The Buckeyes' defense was equally culpable in their defeat, consistently failing to get off the field and allowing Nebraska to run nearly 20 more plays than they could muster. Meanwhile, quarterback Luke Fahey managed to keep his team in contention with a respectable performance, throwing for 259 yards and two touchdowns. Ohio State's season has taken a decidedly downward turn, with the team now sporting an unenviable number of losses - its most since 2011. The circumstances surrounding this decline are all the more surprising given that Ohio State is being led by an interim coach rather than a permanent one. Wake Forest, on the other hand, continues to defy expectations with its dominating performance against Georgia Tech. Although they allowed their first first-half touchdown in four games, the Demon Deacons' overall display was nothing short of ruthless as they emerged victorious 50-29. The Hoosiers' remarkable winning streak came crashing down against Washington, a defeat that has left Indiana facing a precarious situation with two losses on its record - an unfortunate outcome for a team that had been riding high just days prior. The Hoosiers' winning streak came to an abrupt end against Washington, and their playoff prospects are now more uncertain than ever. The team's record has been marred by two losses, a concerning trend for a squad that had been riding high on momentum. Indiana's opponents have proven to be formidable foes, boasting a 23-33 record against Power Four competition. This raises questions about the Hoosiers' ability to compete at the highest level and whether they'll be relegated to the bubble come playoff time. One ranked win against No. 18 USC is their only notable victory. Meanwhile, Oregon's fortunes are on the upswing as quarterback Dylan Raiola led his team to a resounding 45-7 triumph over Michigan State. The highly-rated defense was no match for Raiola, who threw for 234 yards and inspired confidence in his team's ability to compete at the top level. The Ducks' win has propelled them into the Big Ten title race, where they now sit alongside Indiana with a conference record of 6-2. A tiebreaker will decide their fate, pitting them against Iowa in a crucial showdown that could determine which team emerges as a legitimate contender come December. Penn State's loss to Rutgers was nothing short of inexplicable, given the Nittany Lions' commanding lead of 16-0 in the second quarter and 24-10 in the third. The game's final moments saw Antwan Raymond's desperation pass sail into the end zone, courtesy of Ben Black's incredible effort. The home loss has dealt a significant blow to Penn State's aspirations, which had been buoyed by three consecutive victories, including a convincing 42-14 win over Minnesota last week. Now, Campbell's team must navigate a challenging road game against Maryland just to break even and salvage what remains of their season. The Cornhuskers' remarkable turnaround has been years in the making, and it's hard to overlook the significance of their victory against a ranked opponent. Nebraska had faced 31 consecutive losses to teams considered among the best, but Matt Rhule's team finally broke through that barrier. As the clock ticked down, it seemed like fate was working against the Cornhuskers once again. Ohio State, however, managed to mount an impressive drive, covering 75 yards in a matter of minutes to reduce the deficit to just one score. But their momentum was short-lived as they were unable to convert on third-and-five. The Cougars' narrow escape from defeat has left them teetering on the edge of disaster. BYU's inability to hold onto a lead against Kansas, combined with their meager three first-half points in last week's game against Baylor at home, is starting to raise concerns about their ability to sustain momentum. While their victory keeps them in contention for playoff spots, it's clear that the Cougars' historic win over Notre Dame is rapidly receding into memory. The pressure is mounting as they prepare to face new challenges, and a potential drop in the College Football Playoff Rankings threatens to put them right on the chopping block.
